article.title: The end of an era? ANC suffers historic collapse in South Africa
article.author: Zoe Alexandra
article.content: South Africa’s Communist Party just broke away at the ballot box: For the first time since the end of apartheid, the SACP ran on its own ticket in municipal elections, winning 271 seats as Nelson Mandela’s ruling ANC party lost its majority on more than 100 councils – its worst-ever election result. Phel Parkies, the SACP’s national head of elections, joins BT Live to break down the historic shift in South African politics. Parkies says the ANC’s showing reflects the party’s “irreversible decline,” having forfeited the peoples’ trust and confidence through collapsing municipal services and the “voracious accumulation” of corrupt local officials. He says the SACP’s result is a victory for the working class; the party’s mission is socialism in South Africa, “not a consolidation of neoliberalism in our land.” Parkies traces the split back to the ANC’s 1996 adoption of the GEAR economic strategy for “Growth, Employment and Redistribution,” which he says cost the country jobs and deepened inequality: “We believe, as the Communist Party, it was a selling out.” And while the SACP hasn’t left the Tripartite Alliance with the ANC and COSATU, Parkies says it’s now focused on building a broader left unity front – the Conference of the Left – to fight austerity and neoliberalism: “there’s no party that can do that alone.” For the SACP, Parkies says, November 4, 2026 was a turning point: “South Africa is not the same, and it will not be the same.” Watch full episodes of BT Live, join breakthroughnews.org as a member today!
